As inference scales up, in both the number of users and context length, the KV cache can become a bottleneck. The KV cache is the memory store for key and value vectors from previously computed tokens. It allows a model to support long, multi-turn exchanges in a single session without recalculating previous prompts (Figure 1). By using a KV cache to skip computations, the inference engine can deliver a faster TTFT while reducing compute burden on the GPU. ## Executive summary

#### A tiered system for KV cache blocks can turn storage into a strategic advantage [...] Storage-aware tiering. A tiered architecture combines hard drives with SSDs. Hard drives provide durable, high-capacity storage, while SSDs provide active, high-performance storage. Storing KV caches on hard drives reduces re-computation, while using SSDs as a cache layer delivers low-latency transfer.
